title: NCLAT Upholds CIRP Admission Against Shri Paramsukh Edible Foods on GST and TDS Records
case_name: Shri Paramsukh Edible Foods Pvt. Ltd. v. Mohini Food Product
card_summary: The NCLAT dismissed the corporate debtor's appeal against admission of a Section 9 petition. TDS deductions and GST input tax credit entries corroborated the creditor's invoices for mustard seed supplies worth about Rs. 1.42 crore. The debtor's defence, resting on a mismatched e-way bill PIN code, did not amount to a pre-existing dispute, and the admission order stood.
card_tip: Tax records such as TDS deductions and GST input credit entries can corroborate an operational creditor's supply claim; a clerical error in shipping paperwork will rarely by itself defeat admission.
verification_notes: Confirmed from LiveLawBiz's detailed report, which carries the appeal number, bench and reasoning, cross-checked against an independent SupremeToday.ai account of the same ruling; both agree on the parties, the amount claimed and the basis for upholding admission.
